assessments.reasoning: The Commission rendering supplies the v.1.1 heading and notice on page 1, the definition on page 2, the copyleft qualification on page 3 and the acceptance wording on page 4.

The four contiguous acquisition ranges cover all 60,503 bytes and report whole-record SHA-256 96811ec593233b4ea3ce4156bcfe9c693e6e78efb06e7926b892bb926592958a. Part 1 supplies the matching text and part 2 records `licenseId` EUPL-1.1. The template and HTML repeat material from the same record.

The exact SPDX tag object maps v3.29.0 to commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The detail record was opened at that commit. [SPDX tag object](https://api.github.com/repos/spdx/license-list-data/git/tags/76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b)

challenge.method: Compared the pinned `licenseText` with the exact Commission URL and tested substitutions of v.1.0 and v.1.2. Examined the old Joinup references, the release tag and whether a shared clause could produce a false match.
challenge.results: Version 1.0 fails the Articles 1, 5 and 6 comparisons. Version 1.2 shares the essential-functionality wording but has a different heading, an unversioned opening notice and an expanded appendix. The old Joinup links carry `isLive: false` and `match: N/A`. The directly inspected Commission document and SPDX record resolve correspondence without relying on those links.

limitations: The digest observations apply to the SPDX JSON. Original PDF bytes and exact transcription equality were outside the comparison.
The annotated tag is unsigned. Its target is observable in the repository API.

The SPDX release-date comment and the Commission’s adoption recital describe different events. Their chronology was not adjudicated. Language equivalence, redistribution, installation and grants for particular works are outside scope.
reasoning: SPDX release 3.29.0 contains EUPL-1.1 at the stated commit. Its English `licenseText` and the Commission rendering agree on the v.1.1 heading and notice, access to essential functionality in Article 1, the conditional later-version option in Article 5, and acceptance of the licence in Article 6.
